pr_title: fix(docs-infra): several small a11y improvements (including a "skip to content" link)
pr_body:
This PR contains several small accessibility improvements for angular.io (mainly around navigating the page using a keyboard).
See the individual commits for more details.

---
The most impactful change is the addition of a "skip to content" link (last commit):

**fix(docs-infra): add a "skip to content" link for better accessibility**:

Add a link at the top of the page that allows skipping directly to the main content area. This allows people using assistive technologies to skip navigation-related parts of the page which are presented before the main content.

Related resources:
- [www.w3.org](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/G1.html)
- [accessibility.oit.ncsu.edu](https://accessibility.oit.ncsu.edu/it-accessibility-at-nc-state/developers/accessibility-handbook/mouse-and-keyboard-events/skip-to-main-content)
- [css-tricks.com](https://css-tricks.com/how-to-create-a-skip-to-content-link)

##
Example implementations on other websites:

review_comments:
Why is this check needed?
(And should this fix have some associated test?)

Since we are using a different `pathname` for in-page anchors, it is expected that `anchor.href` and `urlParser.href` will be different. For example, if we are on `https://angular.io/docs` and click a link with `href="#main-content"`, `anchor.href` will be `https://angular.io/#main-content` (incorrect), while `urlParser.href` will be `https://angular.io/docs#main-content` (correct).

If `isInPageAnchor` is true, then we know that it is an internal URL (not an external one), so we don't need to infer that by checking if `anchor.href !== urlParser.href`.
And yes, there should be tests 😱 😱 😱

I see. Thanks.

If I remember correctly, we had a workaround in the doc-gen to cope with this scenario, by adding in the current path to all local fragment URLs.

I wonder if we could remove that doc-gen fix, now that the app itself is able to cope?

Yes, we have (a workaround in doc-gen).
And yes, we could (remove it) I think. I'll look into it.

I looked into this and there are a couple of issues:
- The [checkAnchorLinks][1] processor in `dgeni-packages` [tries to resolve links][2] relative to the doc path and `base`, but the [resolveUrl][3] service does not resolve those correctly (i.e. is resolves `#foo` to `/#foo` instead of prepending the current doc's path).
- Our [renderLinkInfo][4] processor [cannot handle][5] URLs starting with `#`.

We could fix these, but I am not sure how much of breaking change it would be to update `resolveUrl()` in `dgeni-packages` to handle `#` links differently (even if arguably more correct 😛).

In any case, since this PR is already approved I am going to mark it for merging and we can make the changes in a follow-up PR.

[1]: https://github.com/angular/dgeni-packages/blob/4e5c3e4eee7d2bb27dd0d419bc7e211635485c3f/base/processors/checkAnchorLinks.js
[2]: https://github.com/angular/dgeni-packages/blob/4e5c3e4eee7d2bb27dd0d419bc7e211635485c3f/base/processors/checkAnchorLinks.js#L75
[3]: https://github.com/angular/dgeni-packages/blob/4e5c3e4eee7d2bb27dd0d419bc7e211635485c3f/base/services/resolveUrl.js#L13
[4]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/7d6ba72b90ba2aa53ee6ce8253cbc90c50e9c9ee/aio/tools/transforms/angular-base-package/processors/renderLinkInfo.js
[5]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/7d6ba72b90ba2aa53ee6ce8253cbc90c50e9c9ee/aio/tools/transforms/angular-base-package/processors/renderLinkInfo.js#L22

It is for interactive elements, but apparently `<a>` without an `href` is not considered interactive by some browsers (rightly so, I guess 😅). So, we need `tabindex` to indicate that this is an interactive element.
